body.cap: Meissa Planet unveiled the forest safety monitoring platform ‘ForestView AI’ at CES 2024 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Meissa Planet (CEO Kim Dong-Young) participated in CES 2024, the world’s largest IT and electronics exhibition in Las Vegas, from the 9th to the 12th.

Meissa Planet has been developing comprehensive solutions in construction, agriculture, forestry, and energy, showcasing high-added value through various spatial technologies, including satellite and drone images.

Differentiating their approach with satellite and drone data fusion, Maisa Planet redefines precision monitoring and survey methods, enhancing safety and efficiency in systems operated by customers with high-quality insights accompanying high-resolution data.

With accumulated expertise in earth observation and analysis, Maisa Planet plans to release its first solution, the ‘ForestView AI platform, in 2024. The company is unveiling the platform for the first time at CES 2024.

ForestView AI, positioned as a forest risk monitoring system, utilizes advanced AI algorithms to detect real-time risks such as forest fires, assisting in effective management. Simultaneously, it provides centralized tools for systematic management through software, contributing to environmental protection and enhancing the sustainability of forestry.

The algorithm of ForestView AI skillfully uses various spatial resolution data to widely observe trends in extensive forests and provides precise and detailed analysis functions for thorough investigation. Through this, it predicts and manages multiple variables such as large and small-scale forest fires, landslides, illegal logging, pest outbreaks, and more.

body.cap: Meissa Planet representatives getting interviewed by AVING News Reporter Jay Kennedy Marcus at CES 2024 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Additionally, ForestView AI has an intuitive interface, offering easy and smooth access for non-experts and general users.

Meissa Planet representative mentioned, “As AI has become a major trend at this year’s CES, visitors exploring the exhibition site have shown interest in ForestView AI, which demonstrates firm value through the convergence of satellite imagery and AI.” They added, “The platform has received acclaim, especially in regions sensitive to forest risks like California, USA. This positive response positions us to evaluate the potential for future global market entry.”

“More than forest monitoring, diverse industries can optimize our AI and satellite-based visual and image data.” They also stated their optimism for future developments. “Having confirmed the expectations and needs in this regard, we will continue to invest our company’s capabilities in new product development, aspiring to evolve into a global spatial information company.”

CES, the world’s largest IT exhibition organized by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), is held in Las Vegas every January, providing a comprehensive view of global innovative technology trends. AVING News, covering CES for 18 consecutive years, has been selecting the best innovative products, companies, and technologies and conducting ‘BEST OF CES’ and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA’ selections. Additionally, through ‘AVING LIVE,’ they provide live coverage of CES issues.

The CES 2024 Seoul Pavilion is being operated on the most historical scale since Seoul’s first participation in CES in 2020, with the largest exhibition area, number of participating companies, and supporter numbers. The Seoul Pavilion, which has collaborated with 13 institutions, is essential in Seoul’s endeavors to establish itself as a startup hub. Among the participating companies in the Seoul Pavilion, 17 received innovation awards, proving their capabilities. Participating institutions include SBA, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul Campus Town, Yangjae Innovation Hub, Gwanak-gu, Yonsei University, Korea University, Chung-Ang University, Sogang University, Kookmin University, Hanyang University, and Kyunghee University, totaling 13. Seoul City and institutions and supporters participating in industry-academic cooperation are matched 1:1 with companies, with a maximum of 85 supporters participating.
